semantic_role_rules.definition: All ordinary reader-facing node-label glyphs at the source 10.1pt node baseline; excludes formula blocks, the trial inline formula, and the application annotation.
Every visible glyph in either source 11.6pt displayed formula block, including the CJK prefix, baseline variables/operators and naturally generated TeX scripts.
Every visible glyph in the source 10.7pt inline formula below the trial node label.
All glyphs in the source 10.1pt application edge annotation.

typographic_class_rules.definition: CJK/full-width reader glyphs; low-stroke CJK remains CJK and is never downgraded.

Latin capitals and digits, plus lowercase letters with an ascender in the predeclared set b,d,f,h,k,l,t. This is a global native-height tier; the original per-glyph minimum-threshold class is retained separately and is not weakened.
Latin lowercase glyphs without ascender or descender; membership is decided from the character before consulting measured pixels.
Latin lowercase letters with a descender in the predeclared set g,j,p,q,y; absent from this figure but defined before mapping.
Baseline lowercase Latin/Greek mathematical variables, excluding operators and natural scripts.
Baseline semantic binary/relation operators from the predeclared set +, minus, =, <, >, <=, >=, multiply and divide.
Baseline uppercase mathematical variables, independent of exact codepoint.
Scripts naturally generated by a >=9.5pt base formula; no entire formula is manually reduced to script style.

singleton_policy: A singleton is not created as a pass escape. It is retained only when a predeclared global semantic/typographic class has one actual member in this figure. Its ratio-to-own-class median is mechanically 1.0, but the report explicitly marks that within-class dispersion is not empirically estimable; source-level role uniformity and the absolute glyph threshold remain mandatory independent gates.
